Build-in-public (DNA social platform - current): https://bsky.app/profile/thaianhsoft.bsky.social (for post technical)

Intro: Self-taught Principal Engineer (7 years). I do not have a CS degree. I learned via MIT OCW in a hospital hallway to pay for my wife's delivery bills. That night, code became my survival mechanism.

Why I am an Outlier:

The "Revenge" Build (Why I built my own IaC SDK) I applied to Pulumi. They loved my technical manifesto but rejected me due to "Wrong Region." I did not give up. I built reactor-dev from scratch in 2-3 months (Drift detection, K8s reconcile loops).

The Validation: A major EV Tech Giant rejected me (no degree), yet they cloned my private repo 13 times to study the architecture. Engineers validated the code, even if HR rejected the person.

Frugal Engineering (The $5 vs $500 Mindset) I am building a social graph backend (DNA Platform) solo. I have no VC money for Cloud DBs.

Solution: I architected a custom Kvrocks + RAMDisk engine with UUIDv7 sorting.

Result: Reduced infra costs from ~$500/mo to $5/mo (100x reduction). 1000 retries dropped to 0.

Resilience I have been rejected by WorldQuant, Nvidia, and Zalo purely for "No Degree." Yet, I continue to ship production-grade distributed systems.

What I am looking for: I am not looking for a "stable job" to hide in. I am looking for a Founder/CTO who values execution over credentials. If you need an engineer who treats your infrastructure budget like their own grocery money, let's talk.

author: cess11
html:
I've been making computers obey for close to four decades, and after a stint as developing CTO/'Founder' in a startup-like environment I'm on the lookout for something new. With me you'll get risk-averse compliant systems and product development with a taste for elegance tempered by both business know-how and experience with public sector organisations.

I'm at my strongest on the backend but have no fear of interfaces. Data wrangling and message passing comes easy for me, and if you want me to I'll learn both new programming languages and complex regulations needed to judge what we can and can't do.

A lot of my work experience has been spent on so called legacy code, so that's something I'm good at. Perhaps there are 2 MLOC ticking away on a server that no one has touched in years, perhaps you just bought a competing product and want to chop out the good parts, I'll sit down and fix it and show up on your screen every now and then and tell you how it goes and what it would require to do it faster. You'll also get diagrams and show-and-tells aimed at people with background in non-technical professions, and documentation that smooths the on-boarding of juniors.

English is fine, born into swedish, if you pay me while I do it I'll dust off my german or spanish and aim for fluency within a year. At work I'm not as grumpy as I might be when posting off here, I'm actually pretty easy-going and quite solution oriented, as it is required when doing the kind of work for lawyers, the government and profitable B2B customers that I have.

If you have financing and would like to build a business doing software due diligence, e.g. towards investors, creditors, bankruptcy lawyers or whatever, then I'd really, really like to come into contact with you. author: TZubiri
html:
So this website is filled mostly with tech founder adjacent users, so my pitch is a bit specific to that market.

If you are a startup founder trying to develop a global product, I'm offering country-specific localization (Argentina currently), everything from language and dialect localization, to integration of local methods and support channels to payment/support aggregators.

Want to dominate the world? Try bottom up, perfecting a single market, instead of top down, aiming everywhere and seeing what sticks.

Why not focus on the US? You can try both for sure, but a smaller country is less competitive and easier to get a big win on (niche domination). You won't make as much money, GDP per capita is about one third of the US, but it's still profit, not VC-backed losses.

I work on a small fixed fee + commission basis. The goal is to only hit it big if you do too, and live on rice otherwise.

If that's sounds interesting, you can send me an email at localization@tomaszubiri.com, sure, but ideally you can write me a message in this thread directly.
